original_value: This paper explores the decision-making and coordination mechanism of pricing and collection rate in a closed-loop supply chain with capacity constraint in recycling channels, which consists of one manufacturer and one retailer. On the basis of game theory, the equilibriums of decisions and profits in the centralized and decentralized scenarios are obtained and compared. Through the performance analysis of a different scenario, a higher saving production cost and lower competition intensity trigger the members to engage in remanufacturing. Furthermore, we try to propose a two-part tariff contract through bargaining to coordinate supply chain and achieve a Pareto improvement. The results show that when the capacity constraints in recycling channels exceed a threshold, the decisions and profit will change. Additionally, for closed-loop supply chain, the selling price is more susceptible to the influence of capacity constraint in recycling channel than the members’ profit.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines pricing and collection-rate decision making, as well as coordination, in a closed-loop supply chain with capacity constraints in the recycling channel, composed of one manufacturer and one retailer. Using game theory, it derives and compares the equilibrium decisions and profits under centralized and decentralized settings. Scenario analysis shows that higher production cost savings and lower competition intensity motivate the members to engage in remanufacturing. The study also proposes a bargained two-part tariff contract to coordinate the supply chain and achieve Pareto improvement. The results indicate that once recycling-channel capacity constraints exceed a threshold, decisions and profits will change. In addition, for the closed-loop supply chain, selling price is more sensitive to recycling-channel capacity constraints than members’ profit.
